title: Macs: are they as locked down as your Windows PCs?
short: Enroll every Mac through Apple Business so it can't leave management, and enforce macOS updates within 7 days, or 72 hours when exploited.
answer: This quarter, enroll every company Mac through Apple Business with locked enrollment, enforce macOS updates with a 7-day deadline and give users standard accounts with FileVault keys escrowed. Then push your EDR's extensions and permissions so users can't remove them, and judge the rest by whether it would stop a pasted Terminal command.
audience: IT and security teams managing company Macs with Intune, Jamf or another MDM

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Enroll every Mac through Apple Business, locked.
items.text: Buy from Apple or an authorized reseller so the serial number lands in Apple Business, free since April 2026[^abnews]. Set **Locked enrollment**[^intuneade]; a registered Mac on macOS 14+ can put off enrollment only once, for 8 hours[^ade].

items.title: Enforce updates with a deadline.
items.text: Use declarative update enforcement: in Intune, **Software Update Enforce Latest** with **Delay in Days** at 7[^intuneupd]. When Apple says a flaw may have been exploited, enforce that version within 72 hours, as the browsers sheet does. Pilot major upgrades first.

items.title: Give users standard accounts.
items.text: Let enrollment create a hidden admin and a standard user. Intune's macOS LAPS gives the admin a 15-character password, rotates it every 6 months and audits each view[^laps].

items.title: Turn on FileVault in Setup Assistant.
items.text: Set **Force Enable in Setup Assistant** with **Defer** enabled (macOS 14+), so Intune escrows the key before encryption starts[^fv]. The BSI says the key must not be stored online with Apple[^bsi].

items.title: Run EDR with permissions users can't undo.
items.text: Preapprove Defender's system extensions and permissions with MDM profiles[^mdemac], and set tamper protection as the endpoints and email sheet says. Set `AllowUserOverrides` to false and list the EDR in `NonRemovableSystemExtensions` (macOS 15+)[^sysext].

blocks.title: Set up a new Mac in this order

items.title: Is the serial number in Apple Business?
items.text: If not, erase the Mac and add it with Apple Configurator for iPhone. The user can still release it within 30 days of enrollment[^abconfig].

items.title: Does setup wait for your policies?
items.text: Turn on **Await final configuration**[^intuneade] and require a minimum macOS version, so Setup Assistant updates the Mac first[^ade].

items.title: How do users sign in?
items.text: Use Platform SSO with the Secure Enclave method: Microsoft counts it as phishing-resistant, and every Intune plan includes it[^psso]. Since macOS 26, MDM can enforce it in Setup Assistant[^wn26]. Okta offers it through Okta Device Access[^okta].

items.title: Which permissions does each tool need?
items.text: Grant Full Disk Access (**System Policy All Files**) with privacy profiles (PPPC); MDM can only deny camera, microphone and screen recording[^pppc]. macOS 27 lets users revoke Accessibility that MDM granted[^wn27].

items.title: Does access depend on compliance?
items.text: Require System Integrity Protection, encryption, Gatekeeper at **Mac App Store and identified developers** and a minimum OS build[^comp]. Then require a compliant device (passkeys and MFA sheet).

blocks.title: Versions and updates in November 2026
items: **Three versions still get fixes.** On 26 October 2026, Apple patched macOS 27.2, Tahoe 26.7.2 and Sequoia 15.8.2; Sonoma's last OS fix came on 6 August[^appsec]. Older versions don't get every fix[^aboutsu], so set an end date for Sequoia.
**Intel Macs can't move to macOS 27.** It runs only on Apple silicon[^appsec]. Budget replacements now: the BSI says Macs without security updates shouldn't be used[^bsi].

**Keep security data updates on.** Force automatic security updates, which carry XProtect and Gatekeeper data. Background Security Improvements apply only to the latest minor version, so a deferral delays them too[^enforce].
**Warn users about the deadline.** When it passes, macOS quits open apps, even with unsaved documents, and restarts if needed[^enforce]. Announce the date a week ahead.

blocks.title: How Macs get infected now
items: **Atomic macOS Stealer leads.** Of the top five stealer families Microsoft Defender Experts saw, it had 50% of the activity, MacSync 7%. Mac-targeted activity has grown since late 2025[^mddr].

**Pasted commands skip Gatekeeper.** Fake troubleshooting guides have users paste a Terminal command that fetches a script with curl. Scripts started from Terminal don't get the checks Gatekeeper runs on apps opened in Finder[^msclickfix].

**Standard accounts don't stop them.** The stealer asks for the user's password, then takes Keychain entries, browser passwords, session cookies and wallets[^msclickfix]. See the browsers sheet on cookie theft.
**The paste warning is a speed bump.** It appears only when someone who rarely uses Terminal pastes a command from a website, chat or email, and they can choose Paste Anyway[^paste].

**Gatekeeper overrides moved.** Since Sequoia, users allow unnotarized apps in Privacy & Security, not with Control-click[^sequoia]. On macOS 15+, Endpoint Security tools can log each bypass[^xprotect].

blocks.title: When a Mac is lost or compromised
items: **Lost: lock it.** A remote lock restarts the Mac and asks for a six-digit PIN. Managed Lost Mode, with location, is only for iPhone and iPad[^lock].
**Compromised: isolate it.** Isolate it in Defender[^mdemac] and follow the incident response sheet. Assume the Keychain, browser passwords and cookies are stolen[^msclickfix], and reset them.

**Erase and re-enroll.** MDM erase uses Erase All Content and Settings; on Apple silicon it needs a bootstrap token[^erase]. Rotate a FileVault key or admin password after anyone views it[^fv][^laps].

**Keep Activation Lock in your hands.** Leave it off unless MDM holds the bypass code, via **Activation Lock Allowed While Supervised**[^intuneal]. Apple Business can lift a user's lock on Macs added before it was on[^abal].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Letting the first user be admin.** Without a managed admin account, the Setup Assistant account must be one[^laps].
**Counting on that admin for FileVault.** Intune's LAPS admin gets no secure token[^laps]; keep the escrowed key.
**Requiring a password in a compliance policy.** It expires every password on the Mac, LAPS and Platform SSO accounts included[^comp].
**Exempting developers.** Mac stealer campaigns aim at cloud and developer environments[^mddr].
**Wiping before copying the bypass code.** Intune deletes it at reset[^intuneal]. Add the step to the laptop return in the joiners and leavers sheet.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Apple Business replaced Apple Business Manager.** Since 14 April 2026, it is free and includes a built-in MDM[^abnews].
**macOS 27 dropped Intel and legacy update management.** Since 14 September 2026, it runs only on Apple silicon[^appsec] and ignores MDM update commands[^wn27].
**macOS 27 can block binaries.** Supervised Macs can enforce allow or deny lists through a built-in Endpoint Security client[^allowdeny].
**Intune ended legacy Setup Assistant authentication.** Since October 2026, profiles use modern authentication[^intuneade]; test it now.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A second antivirus beside the EDR.** Defender for Endpoint on Mac includes antivirus[^mdemac], on top of XProtect's signatures[^xprotect].
**Binding Macs to Active Directory.** Platform SSO can map on-premises Kerberos tickets from Entra ID[^pssoscen].
**Blocking Terminal for everyone.** Developers and IT need it. EDR and binary control cover the risk better.

**BSI steps older than Apple silicon.** SYS.2.4 asks for NVRAM and SMC resets and a firmware password[^bsi]. On Apple silicon, erasing makes data cryptographically inaccessible[^erase] and FileVault replaces the password[^fwpw].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Without Intune or Jamf, start with Apple Business's free built-in MDM[^abnews].
Run Defender for Business on every Mac, as the endpoints and email sheet says.
Ask your reseller to register every Mac in Apple Business.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Grant admin rights for minutes, with a reason: Jamf Connect's Self Service+ defaults to 5[^jamfpe]; SAP's Privileges is open source[^privileges].
Report weekly per Mac: macOS version, escrowed key, EDR health.
Switch MDM without a wipe: Apple Business migrates macOS 26 Macs[^wn26].

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Generate a CIS Level 1 baseline and MDM profiles with NIST's mSCP, updated for each macOS release[^mscp].
Pilot binary allow lists for admins and finance.
Map your profiles to BSI SYS.2.4 for audits[^bsi].

changes.text: Published after a copy edit and a source-by-source fact check, which aligned the update deadline for exploited flaws with the browsers sheet, scoped Microsoft's stealer figures and the paste warning to what the sources say and narrowed the Intune enrollment change to authentication.

First draft, based on Apple Platform Deployment and Apple Business documentation, Microsoft Learn pages on Intune and Defender for Endpoint on Mac, the Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026, Microsoft's macOS ClickFix research and BSI SYS.2.4.
